messages:
alex: Heads-up — ACME reported a sharp p99 jump on /v1/generate around 14:10Z. Dashboard p99 = 4200ms but raw histogram shows >95% requests <200ms. attaching their repro steps and the dashboard query they used. can we figure out whether this is a rollup vs raw origin mismatch?

priya: Customer says it started right after they hit a spike of 10k reqs/min, some 500s and retries showed up in their logs. They provided trace ids. Ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/ACME-9876 :grimacing:

maya: likely suspects: (1) rollup windowing + late-arriving samples, (2) auth-proxy retry traffic being bubbled into the same metric without a retry label, (3) different metric origin for dashboard panel vs histogram. quickly: what query does the dashboard use?

alex: dashboard panel uses our p99 rollup metric: redwood_latency_p99_rollup{route="/v1/generate"} while histogram panel uses redwood_http_latency_bucket{route="/v1/generate"}. both panels are for prod-us. customer also ran a raw prometheus query and sent a screenshot.

jamal: If the rollup uses ingestion_time or rollup_ts instead of event_time we can see a short-lived tail when batch reorder happens. Also auth-proxy retries can create long tails if the proxy emits a metric for the aggregate attempt.

priya: They pulled an individual trace:
```
trace: 2023-11-02T14:09:58Z span gen -> auth-proxy retry -> backend 1.8s -> retry -> backend 3.9s total ~6.1s
trace-id: acme-xxxx-999
```
They said the dashboard p99 lined up exactly with that trace window.

maya: ok can someone grep for label "retry=true" or check for origin labels? run:
```
# check distinct origins
count by (origin) (redwood_http_latency_bucket{route="/v1/generate"})
# check retries
sum(rate(redwood_request_total{route="/v1/generate",retry!=""}[5m]))
```

jamal: quick repro steps from my side (local):
1) run a small proxy that retries on 502
2) send parallel requests with intermittent 502 from backend
3) observe metrics: proxy emits request_count without retry label -> p99 rollup inflates

Commands:
```
# fire load
for i in {1..2000}; do curl -s -H "x-test: retry" http://localhost:8080/v1/generate & done
```

deploy-bot: deployment redwood/auth-proxy v2.14.1 -> prod-us completed at 2023-11-02T14:05Z (sha: ab12cd).

alex: that matches timeline. new proxy release changed retry behavior to emit metrics earlier (and it does not set retry label). so rollup that ingests those early samples will see a tail.

maya: mitigation options:
- short-term: update dashboard to compare rollup p99 vs histogram p99 side-by-side and add an annotation for deploy time
- medium: change rollup pipeline to prefer event_time when available, or drop samples missing retry label for p99 rollups
- long-term: ensure proxy sets retry=true label and rollup code ignores proxy-internal attempts

jamal: I can push a quick guard to rollup (reject samples where source="proxy" and header x-internal-retry present) — low risk.

priya: please confirm before I update customer. they want ETA and whether this is user-facing.

alex: jamal, can you open a PR with a config flag to ignore proxy-internal attempts? maya can review the observability implications. mark hotfix.

jamal: will do, PR in ~30m. gonna add a dashboard diff and a small synthetic test that simulates retries.

maya: i'll add a temporary dashboard widget that shows the delta (rollup_p99 - histogram_p99) and an alert if > 500ms for 5m. also add deploy annotation.

priya: customer update drafted: "we see your traces and a proxy deploy at 14:05 likely caused the spike; engineers are rolling a small rollup guard to exclude proxy-internal retry samples; will follow up with timeline and PR." ok?

alex: yep send it. include link to ticket and note it's not a regression in model runtime — it's observability aggregation.

priya: sent. they replied :thumbsup: and asked for ETA.

jamal: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rollup/pull/239 — adds ignore_proxy_retries flag and unit tests. requesting maya review.

maya: reviewing now. small comment on metric cardinality handling. aside: we should audit other proxies for similar behavior.

alex: thanks all. follow-ups: jamal -> merge hotfix, maya -> temp alert + dashboard, priya -> close customer loop when deployed. leaving channel for visibility. :rocket:
